# ink

> A terminal markdown reader that actually looks good.

ink is a command-line tool that renders markdown files in the terminal with rich formatting. Built in Rust as a single binary with no runtime dependencies.

## What it does

- Renders markdown with syntax highlighting, tables, blockquotes, lists, task lists, footnotes, and horizontal rules
- Displays inline images using terminal graphics protocols (Kitty, iTerm2, Sixel) where supported, falling back to Unicode half-block characters (any true-color terminal); --image-protocol selects the renderer
- Renders mermaid diagrams (flowcharts, sequence diagrams, pie charts, Gantt charts) as ASCII art
- Supports GitHub-style admonitions: NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION
- Supports wikilink syntax: [[page]] and [[page|display text]]
- Renders inline/block math ($...$, $$...$$) in code style and resolves :emoji: shortcodes
- Interactive TUI with multi-tab support, in-document search (n/N to cycle matches), keyboard link opening (press f), a help overlay (?), and a table of contents sidebar
- File browser mode for exploring directories of markdown files
- 8 built-in color themes with auto dark/light detection, live theme picker that saves to config, plus custom TOML themes
- Presentation mode (split on --- separators), navigate with arrows/space
- Watch mode for live-reloading on file changes
- Pager mode: `ink --plain` on a TTY pages long output through $PAGER (like bat)
- Honors NO_COLOR and downgrades to 256-color on non-truecolor terminals
- Document statistics, outline view, and a real (Myers) markdown diff
- Vim-style keybindings (j/k/G/Ctrl+f/Ctrl+b), also emacs preset, fully customizable
- Reads from files, URLs, or stdin
- Plain output mode for piping (ANSI-colored, no TUI)
- Shell completions (bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell/elvish) and a man page

## Security

- Sanitizes terminal control/escape bytes out of untrusted markdown before rendering (both TUI and --plain), preventing ANSI/OSC escape-sequence and hyperlink injection
- Remote (http/https) images are not fetched by default; --remote-images opts in, and private/loopback/cloud-metadata addresses stay blocked
- URL fetches are timeout- and size-capped; relative file/link paths are contained to the document's directory
- install.sh verifies a published SHA256SUMS manifest before installing

## Install

cargo install ink-md

## Usage

ink README.md            # read a file
ink .                    # browse markdown files in current directory
ink --plain file.md      # pipe-friendly ANSI output (pages via $PAGER on a TTY)
ink --slides deck.md     # presentation mode
ink --watch draft.md     # auto-reload on changes
ink --remote-images x.md # allow remote images (off by default)
ink --list-themes        # list available themes
ink outline file.md      # show heading structure
ink stats file.md        # word count, reading time
ink diff a.md b.md       # compare two files (Myers diff)
ink completions zsh      # shell completions
ink man                  # man page
